acceptance_basis: Full-length ceiling compounded from P-BLOCK-PUR over P-N-BLOCKS (EQ-PURITY). An assumption, not a specification.
notes: The first anchor point, as data: this is the control that sets the purity ceiling, and it sits OUTSIDE the facility. No downstream separation can raise it, because block-internal n-1 differs from the product by one nucleotide in the middle of a strand. No in-facility instrument enforces it - the enforcement is an incoming specification and a supplier certificate. The measured basis is 89-96 percent for 4-5 nt modified blocks (SRC-WO2020227618), which are NOT our 5'-phosphate blocks (Q-011). A route that omits capping makes this worse by converting coupling failures into deletions rather than truncations (R-018).

acceptance_basis: P-LIG-CONV per ligation, compounded over the assembly (EQ-LIG). Assumption.
notes: Conversion is what decides how much whole-block impurity is introduced, and unlike the block floor it IS adjustable in-facility. The cited figure is per-ligation, not a step mass yield (P-YLD-LIG), and it comes from a 5 mL packed column at 600 uM - a different scale and a different enzyme format from a kg-scale batch (Q-010, Q-050).

cpp: ATP concentration in the ligation reaction
acceptance_basis: P-LIG-ATP as charged into the ligation buffer. Assumption, and a CONTESTED one.
notes: This row is where the control strategy contradicts itself and says so. A four-ligation assembly wants at least 4 mM ATP (SRC-WO2025262452); suppressing the adenylylated dead end wants two orders of magnitude less (SRC-PBCV1-2014). No source reconciles them, the optimum moves with the enzyme form (Q-050), and the dead end it produces cannot be filtered out afterwards (R-010). The acceptance basis is therefore a placeholder with a live conflict attached, not a setpoint (Q-040).

Both cited ligation examples ran at the same temperature, in two different regimes with two different enzymes - agreement, but not a demonstrated optimum for ours (Q-050). A higher setpoint would also move the reaction closer to the duplex melting band (P-DS-TM, Q-030, R-003), so this parameter is bounded from above by a limit nobody has measured for our sequence.

acceptance_basis: The reaction is held to a conversion endpoint, not to a clock. P-LIG-TIME is the band that has been demonstrated, and is an expectation rather than a limit.
notes: The instrument named here is the conversion IPC, not a timer, and that is the point: a hold time is an outcome of the reaction reaching its endpoint. The band brackets two different enzymes at two different temperatures, and whether a batch hold is even the right regime depends on the enzyme form - an immobilised route is a packed-column residence time instead (Q-050, Q-010).

BLANK acceptance basis, deliberately. Stating a loading here would silently choose an enzyme form, and that choice is open (Q-050). This row exists because it SIZES the clearance problem two rows below: the one cited loading is a cell-free-extract loading, which puts a whole proteome plus endotoxin through purification rather than one enzyme (R-017). The loading is set by what is charged, so no instrument measures it directly - the two named instruments measure its consequence in the clarified pool.

NO CONTROL IS DEFINED, and this row says so rather than implying one. The proposed mitigation is to suppress AppN at the reaction by lowering ATP, but that pulls directly against the ATP a multi-ligation assembly needs (Q-040) - so the mitigation in R-010 is a direction, not a control. The instrument named can SEE the species; nothing in this register prevents it. The dead end differs from the product by about 329 Da, so filtration cannot remove it downstream.

cpp: Powder glass transition at the achieved residual moisture
notes: The BINDING thermal limit on drying and storage, and the second anchor point as data. BLANK acceptance basis: the glass transition is a function of OUR matrix and OUR achieved moisture (EQ-TG, Gordon-Taylor), and neither is fixed - the excipient ratio is open (Q-021) and so is where the excipient enters (Q-038). The band that exists was measured on spray-dried trehalose siRNA polyplex formulations at their own moisture, not ours (Q-039). The pair of parameters travels together because a glass transition quoted without the moisture it was measured at is detached from its condition.

acceptance_basis: Outlet gas temperature held below the duplex melting temperature, as a conservative proxy for the particle (P-DRY-T-OUT below P-DS-TM). The LOOSER of the two thermal limits.
notes: The relation is the acceptance basis; the bound is not known. The melting band that exists is for a 21-mer with three modified positions in 100 mM NaCl, not our fully modified duplex, and the authors' per-position increment must not be extrapolated across all 21 positions (Q-030). The outlet setpoint itself is an assumption (Q-046). Tier 2 stated this limit as the duplex control; it is the looser one - the glass transition above binds first (Q-039).

cpp: Final diafiltration matrix and excipient ratio
acceptance_basis: Final diafiltration exchanges into a spray-dryable matrix at P-EXCIPIENT-RATIO. Assumption.
notes: The third leg of the duplex-integrity argument: the matrix sets the glass transition the row above is measured against (EQ-TG). Non-volatile buffer salts concentrate through evaporation into the powder unless the final exchange removes them (R-005). The ratio is a placeholder (Q-021) and where the excipient enters swings the evaporation duty severalfold (Q-038), so this row is a formulation choice standing in for a formulation decision nobody has made.

cpp: Ligase clearance - soluble branch, denature then depth filtration
cqa: Residual enzyme protein in the drug substance
notes: ONE OF TWO BRANCHES, NEITHER CHOSEN. Blank acceptance: no log-reduction, ppm or immunoassay figure for ligase clearance exists in the public record for either branch (Q-032). This branch is not free - the cited denature condition is a heat kill well above any plausible duplex melting band, which trades an enzyme-clearance gap for a product-integrity risk (R-021, P-DS-TM, Q-030) - and the cited route follows the heat kill with an ion column rather than filtration alone (R-002). It also needs a heated vessel or exchanger that DOES NOT EXIST in the equipment register: U02-CF is single-use depth media and cannot denature anything. That missing unit is registered against Q-050 rather than invented here.

cpp: Ligase clearance - immobilised branch, retention on the carrier
cqa: Residual enzyme protein in the drug substance
notes: THE OTHER BRANCH, EQUALLY UNCHOSEN. Blank acceptance for the same reason. The one demonstrated immobilised route uses IMAC-type non-covalent immobilisation, the format most prone to leaching, so retention on the carrier is the claim that would have to be demonstrated rather than the one that can be assumed (Q-032, Q-050). If it fails, enzyme removal reverts to chromatography and the filtration-led thesis breaks (R-002).

cpp: In-line concentration measurement at the UF/DF endpoint
notes: THE ROW THIS WHOLE SLICE EXISTS TO MAKE EXPRESSIBLE. There is no in-line concentration control here, because there is no in-line instrument: UV saturates on a 21-mer at process concentration - the path length required is about 10 um - and the answer deployed in the field is variable-pathlength slope spectroscopy, which is AT-line (Q-042). The named instrument is that at-line substitute; it is a measurement, not a control loop, and it is named here so the reader can see what stands in place of the control. The tech-transfer page advertised in-line UV on UF/DF as PAT for two tiers while Q-042 recorded the opposite in the same repository, and nothing in the repo could see the contradiction until control_type could say not_measurable.
